System design · Review deck

Review deck: System design

Every quiz question and memory hook in this track, as flashcards. Answer in your head, reveal, then say how well you knew it. Cards you find hard come back soon; cards you know well wait days, then weeks. Ten minutes a day keeps everything you've learned within reach.

1. Review now

Keys: space reveals the answer; 1–4 grade it. Progress is saved in this browser only (nothing is sent anywhere); clearing site data resets it.

2. How it works

This is spaced repetition: reviewing just before you'd forget is the most efficient way to make knowledge stick. Each card sits in a box from 0 to 6. "Good" moves it up a box and schedules it further out (1, 3, 7, 16, 35, then 90 days); "Easy" jumps two boxes; "Hard" keeps it in its box and brings it back sooner; "Again" sends it back to box 0 and shows it again in this session. A card counts as learned from box 3.

Say it before you reveal

Answer out loud or on paper first. Recognising the answer after seeing it feels like knowing it, but isn't.

Little and often

Ten minutes daily beats an hour on Sunday. The schedule only works if you come back when cards are due.

Go back to the page

Every card links to its page. If you keep missing one, reread that section and run its visualizer again.
